title: REWRITE of a record in a z/OS UNIX byte-stream file read through QSAM (the file cannot be open I-O): file status 49
shapes: AIXA AIXAUXR: SELECT UR-FILE ASSIGN TO UXRWR ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL; 0000-MAIN OPEN OUTPUT, WRITE, REWRITE, PERFORMs 1000-CHECK (tests '49')
asserts: The SELECT is one file_control fact (select UR-FILE, assign UXRWR, organization SEQUENTIAL, access_mode SEQUENTIAL, record_key null) with no alternate_keys and no relative_key. 1000-CHECK is one units fact, PERFORMed once from 0000-MAIN as a plain edges fact, and tests the FILE STATUS item named in the SELECT. DD UXRWR in step UR9191 is a jcl_dds fact with dsn null, no sysout and no disp (PATH= is a z/OS UNIX file, as in H-0137). At run time the OPEN OUTPUT and the WRITE succeed; the REWRITE cannot update a file in the z/OS UNIX file system, and since such a file can never be open I-O it ends in file status 49 (REWRITE on a file not open I-O); the program takes the 49 branch and WS-BAD stays 0. Step UR9191 has three jcl_dds facts: STEPLIB, UXRWR and SYSOUT.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Programming Guide (SC27-8714-03)
citations.section: Coding input and output statements for QSAM files > REWRITE
citations.quote: You cannot update a file in the z/OS UNIX file system using REWRITE.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Programming Guide (SC27-8714-03)
citations.section: Coding input and output statements for QSAM files > OPEN
citations.quote: You cannot open z/OS UNIX files as I-O; a file status of 37 results if you attempt to do so.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: The execution of a DELETE or REWRITE statement was attempted on a file not open in the I-O mode.

notes: The 49 is an inference from two quoted rules, not a sentence IBM prints: the Programming Guide says REWRITE cannot update a UNIX file and that such a file cannot be opened I-O (37), and Table 34 gives 49 for REWRITE on a file not open I-O; the manual does not name the status for this exact statement. Status 47 is not used for this case: Table 34 gives 47 to READ and START on a file not open input or I-O, not to REWRITE. The outcome assumes the OPEN OUTPUT of the PATH succeeds (PATHOPTS OWRONLY,OCREAT,OTRUNC and PATHMODE give the program write access to /u/aixa/extract). The FD's record layout is nominal. GnuCOBOL statuses were not compared.
